data.content:
120	  chart value.  For the Abel chart this is `chartLocus`;
   121	* `r` recovers the chart point: over `W`, the divisor family whose class `g` is;
   122	* `sq` says the two ways round agree;
   123	* `exists_factor` is the honest content — a test point of `X` and a test point of `T` with
   124	  the *same* class come from a unique point of `W`.  Existence is coverage-on-the-locus;
   125	  the uniqueness half is *not* a field here, because it is free: `W.ι` is a monomorphism.
   126	
   127	Nothing in this structure mentions a divisor scheme, a certificate, a twist or a chart
   128	index.  It is a statement about a morphism of presheaves and an open of a test. -/
   129	structure ChartFibrePresented {X T : Scheme.{u}}
   130	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   131	    where
   132	  /-- The locus of the test where the class named by `g` is a chart value. -/
   133	  W : T.Opens
   134	  /-- The chart point over that locus. -/
   135	  r : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X
   136	  /-- The square commutes: `r` names the class `g` restricted to `W`. -/
   137	  sq : yoneda.map r ≫ f = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   138	  /-- **Coverage on the locus**: an `S`-point of `X` and an `S`-point of `T` carrying the
   139	  same class factor through `W`, compatibly with both projections. -/
   140	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (v : S ⟶ X) (w : S ⟶ T),
   141	    f.app (op S) v = g.app (op S) w → ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}), u ≫ r = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   142	
   143	namespace ChartFibrePresented
   144	
   145	variable {X T : Scheme.{u}} {f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
   146	  {g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1}
   147	
   148	/-- **The datum presents the fibre product**: the square of `ChartFibrePresented` is a
   149	pullback of presheaves.
   150	
   151	Pullbacks in a presheaf category are computed pointwise
   152	(`IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app`), and a pointwise pullback of types is exactly
   153	"commutes + jointly injective + jointly surjective" (`Types.isPullback_iff`).  The first is
   154	`sq`, the third is `exists_factor`, and the second is free from `W.ι` being a
   155	monomorphism — which is where the openness of `W` does its work. -/
   156	theorem isPullback (D : ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
   157	    IsPullback (yoneda.map D.r) (yoneda.map D.W.ι) f g := by
   158	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   159	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   160	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   161	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 =>
   162	      φ.app S) D.sq
   163	  · -- joint injectivity: already forced by `W.ι` alone, being a monomorphism
   164	    rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   165	    have : u₁ ≫ D.W.ι = u₂ ≫ D.W.ι := h₂
   166	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp this
   167	  · -- joint surjectivity: `exists_factor` at the test `S.unop`
   168	    intro v w hvw
   169	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   170	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
   171	
   172	end ChartFibrePresented
   173	
   174	/-- **THE CRITERION** — `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` from elementwise data, discharging BOTH
   175	clauses of `MorphismProperty.relative` at once.
   176	
   177	Given, for every test point of the target sheaf, a `ChartFibrePresented` datum, the chart map
   178	is an open immersion of presheaves.  Certificate-free, divRep-free, and with no reference to
   179	divisors: the input is a family of opens of tests together with the coverage statement on
   180	each.
   181	
   182	This is the honest shape of `IsChartUniv`'s obligation.  Reading `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf`
   183	as a single "relative GAP-2" statement conflates:
   184	
   185	* **relative representability** — that the fibre product is a scheme at all.  Supplied here
   186	  by `W`, an open subscheme of the test, and proved by `ChartFibrePresented.isPullback`;
   187	* **the property clause** — that each represented pullback is an open immersion.  Supplied
   188	  here by `W.ι` being an open immersion, which is free.
   189	
   190	What is *not* free, and is the whole mathematical content, is `exists_factor`: a class that
   191	agrees with a chart value must come from the locus.  For the Abel chart that is the relative
   192	form of DAT-C GAP-2 (uniqueness of the normalized effective representative) fed through the
   193	classifier — so the CERT-Σ gate is real, but it gates ONE field of ONE structure rather than
   194	the whole certificate. -/
   195	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
   196	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   197	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
   198	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) :
   199	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
   200	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists fun T g => ?_
   201	  exact ⟨(D T g).W, yoneda.map (D T g).r, (D T g).W.ι, (D T g).isPullback,
   202	    inferInstance⟩
   203	
   204	/-! ## The criterion is not vacuous
   205	
   206	A structure whose hard field is an existential can be inhabited for trivial reasons, and a
   207	criterion built on one is then worthless.  This section rules that out **by proof** rather
   208	than by inspection: the datum is unconstructible exactly when it must be. -/
   209	
   210	/-- **Non-vacuity of `ChartFibrePresented`, from the necessary direction.**
   211	
   212	If a chart map fails to be injective on the points of even one test, then no family of
   213	`ChartFibrePresented` data exists for it.  In particular the criterion cannot be satisfied
   214	for the *unrestricted* Abel chart, whose non-injectivity is the linear system `|D|`
   215	(`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`): the criterion's hypothesis is genuinely as strong as the
   216	conclusion, and `exists_factor` is not a clause one can talk one's way past.
   217	
   218	The proof composes the two halves of this file, which is the point of having both. -/
   219	theorem isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
   220	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ)
   221	    (hT : ¬ Function.Injective (f.app T)) :
   222	    IsEmpty (∀ (T' : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T' ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
   223	        ChartFibrePresented C f g) :=
   224	  ⟨fun D => hT (injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
   225	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T)⟩
   226	
   227	/-- The same statement in the form a lane will meet it: the criterion's input **implies**
   228	elementwise injectivity on every test.  So a lane that cannot prove uniqueness of the
   229	normalized effective representative cannot supply the datum either — the CERT-Σ gate is not
   230	an artefact of how `IsChartUniv` was pinned. -/
   231	theorem injective_of_chartFibrePresented {X : Scheme.{u}}
   232	    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   233	    (D : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
   234	      ChartFibrePresented C f g) (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
   235	    Function.Injective (f.app T) :=
   236	  injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf
   237	    (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented f D) T
   238	
   239	end
   240	
   241	end AlgebraicGeometry

    11	/-!
    12	# The fibre criterion at the RESTRICTED chart, and the `V`-coupling to coverage
    13	
    14	`Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` reduces `IsChartUniv` — antecedent 1 of
    15	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` — to `IsChartLocusFibre`.  **That reduction passes through the
    16	unrestricted certificate, which the project's headers assert to be false**, and this file is
    17	the repair.
    18	
    19	## The defect, measured
    20	
    21	`IsChartLocusFibre` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:166`) asks for a
    22	`ChartFibrePresented C (abelSigmaChart …) g` at every test — the datum for the *unrestricted*
    23	chart, with `W` a free structure field.  Nothing pins `W := chartLocus`, although the docstring
    24	there says the `W` field "is already discharged — it is `chartLocus`".  So the open `V` never
    25	enters the hypothesis, and one term gives back the unrestricted certificate:
    26	
    27	```
    28	isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
    29	  : IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (abelSigmaChart …)
    30	```
    31	
    32	That measurement is **not** repeated here: it is landed as
    33	`isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` and
    34	`mono_abelSigmaChart_of_isChartLocusFibre` in `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean`, together
    35	with `not_isChartLocusFibre_of_not_injective` — the criterion's own emptiness guard, finally
    36	instantiated at the Abel chart.  In `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` the restriction to `V` is
    37	applied *after* the unrestricted certificate is in hand, so restricting buys nothing on the way
    38	in.
    39	
    40	**The precise status of "false".**  `Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean:54`, `Pic0ChartPair.lean:14` and
    41	`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:214` all assert that the Abel chart is not injective (the
    42	linear system `|D|`), and by the guard above that assertion makes `IsChartLocusFibre`
    43	unsatisfiable.  But **no declaration proves the non-injectivity**: the guard takes
    44	`¬ Function.Injective` as a hypothesis.  So `IsChartLocusFibre` is *conditionally* unsatisfiable
    45	— dead if the headers are right, and nobody has shown they are.  This file therefore does not
    46	claim the old route is dead; it claims the old route is gated on a proposition the project
    47	believes false and has never checked, which is reason enough not to build on it.
    48	
    49	The criterion itself is **not** at fault: it is stated for an arbitrary morphism of presheaves
    50	and is correct.  What was wrong is the *instantiation* — at `abelSigmaChart` rather than at
    51	`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) V`.
    52	
    53	## What this file provides
    54	
    55	* `RestrictedChartFibre` — the same datum demanded at the **restricted** chart, so
    56	  `exists_factor` only has to factor test points *of `V`*.
    57	* `isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre` — it gives `IsChartUniv` at that same `V`, one
    58	  application of the existing criterion, with no unrestricted certificate in between.
    59	* `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` — the weakening did not delete the content: the restricted
    60	  datum still forces injectivity of the restricted chart on every test.
    61	* `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` — **the `V`-coupled assembly** (inbox `I-0861`):
    62	  per-index restricted fibre data on the `hf` side, and on the coverage side the containment
    63	  hypothesis `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, together give the
    64	  representation.  The two sides are made to share the same `V` by typing.
    65	
    66	## Division of labour with the two sibling files landed the same round
    67	
    68	`Pic0ChartLocusFibreGuard.lean` records why the *old* route must not be used, and
    69	`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean` supplies the **coverage** half of the `V`-coupling
    70	(`liftPointwiseToOpens`, and the converse `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` showing `hV` is
    71	exactly the gap).  This file supplies the **`hf`** half — the fibre datum at the restricted
    72	chart — and the assembly that consumes both.  Nothing here re-proves either sibling.
    73	
    74	## The honest limits, stated rather than left for a reviewer
    75	
    76	* **Nothing here produces any input.**  This file replaces a badly-gated route by a
    77	  well-gated one; it discharges no antecedent.  `rep` (divisor representability) is a hypothesis
    78	  throughout, and `IsChartUniv` is not even statable without it.
    79	* **`RestrictedChartFibre` at `V = ⊥` IS inhabited — settled in
    80	  `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`, and an earlier draft of this section priced it
    81	  wrongly.**  That draft said the `sq` field needs
    82	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a₁))` over an empty base, "the triviality of `picEt`
    83	  over the empty scheme: true, a genuinely separate lemma, and absent from the tree", and
    84	  concluded that *no satisfiability witness exists at any `V`*.  **Both the pricing and the
    85	  conclusion were false.**  The error was in the reduction, not the census: the `congr 1` that
    86	  peeled the Σ-component and named `pic0Subgroup` threw away the fact that `pic0SigmaSheaf` is a
    87	  **sheaf**, and a sheaf's value at a scheme covered by the empty sieve is terminal.  So the goal
    88	  is closed by `Sheaf.isTerminalOfBotCover` applied to `Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`
    89	  (both mathlib) with no fact about `picEt` at all — `restrictedChartFibre_bot`.  The
    90	  `exists_factor` half is free as `I-0861` measured; `sq` is free for a different and cheaper
    91	  reason than that draft supposed.
    92	* **Consequence, and it is the sharp form:** the class is non-empty, so the repaired route is not
    93	  a route to an uninhabitable hypothesis, and the unmeasured-inhabitation risk that `ChartTyping`
    94	  (`I-0779`) and `IsChartLocusFibre` carried does **not** apply here.  What that inhabitant also
    95	  shows is that `IsChartUniv` at `V = ⊥` is free (`isChartUniv_bot`) — antecedent 1 carries no
    96	  content in isolation — while the coverage clause is *refuted* at that same value
    97	  (`not_coverageContainment_bot`), and at the other end `V = ⊤` the prices are swapped: coverage's
    98	  containment becomes free and this datum returns the unrestricted certificate.  So the obligation
    99	  is the *coupling*, and any `V` that works must be a proper intermediate open.
   100	* **What that does NOT establish, since a draft of this file claimed it did** (`I-1012`): the two
   101	  endpoints are **not** a non-vacuity check for the assembly below.  Two *bad* values of `V` are
   102	  two refutations; non-vacuity of the pair needs a `V` where both clauses hold.  Inhabitation of
   103	  the **pair** is still unmeasured at every `V`, and `necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre` is not
   104	  that check either.  Only `RestrictedChartFibre` *alone* is now known inhabited.
   105	* **The relation to the old form IS measured, and an earlier draft mispriced it.**  That draft
   106	  said the transport `IsChartLocusFibre → RestrictedChartFibre` "needs the preimage `r ⁻¹ V`
   107	  pushed forward along `W.ι`, which is real work and buys nothing".  Both halves were wrong
   108	  (`I-0936`): it is `restrictedChartFibre_of_isChartLocusFibre` below, twelve lines, needing only
   109	  `IsOpenImmersion.lift` — and it buys the sharp statement, because its hypothesis is exactly the
   110	  coverage half's `hV`.  The "buys nothing" clause was the worse error: a lane holding the old
   111	  form gets `IsChartUniv` *through the certificate three headers call false*, which is this
   112	  file's whole premise.
   113	-/
   114	
   115	set_option autoImplicit false
   116	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
   117	
   118	universe u
   119	
   120	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
   121	
   122	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   123	
   124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   125	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
   126	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   127	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   128	
   129	noncomputable section
   130	
   131	/-! ## The datum at the restricted chart -/
   132	
   133	variable (C π n) in
   134	/-- **The fibre datum demanded at the restricted chart** — the repair of `IsChartLocusFibre`.
   135	
   136	Identical to `IsChartLocusFibre` except that the presented morphism is
   137	`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) V` rather than `abelSigmaChart …`.  The difference is the
   138	whole point: `exists_factor` now only factors test points *of `V`*, so proving it does not
   139	entail that the unrestricted Abel chart is a monomorphism.
   140	
   141	`V` is a parameter and no choice is privileged here; the intended instantiation is the chart
   142	locus, whose openness is CHART-U(b) and a separate obligation. -/
   143	def RestrictedChartFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   144	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   145	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   146	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   147	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   148	    (V : D.left.Opens) : Prop :=
   149	  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
   150	    Nonempty (ChartFibrePresented C
   151	      (restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V) g)
   152	
   153	/-- **The repaired reduction**: the restricted datum gives `IsChartUniv` at the same `V`.
   154	
   155	One application of the existing criterion, at the restricted chart.  Compare
   156	`isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre`, which applies it at the unrestricted chart and composes
   157	afterwards — and therefore needs the unrestricted certificate on the way in. -/
   158	theorem isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   159	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   160	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   161	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   162	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   163	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V) :
   164	    IsChartUniv C π n rep m Z hdeg V :=
   165	  isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented _ fun T g => (h T g).some
   166	
   167	/-- The restricted datum forces the restricted chart to be injective on every test.
   168	
   169	**This is NOT a non-vacuity check, and an earlier draft of this file claimed it was**
   170	(`I-0937`).  Two reasons it does not carry that weight: its conclusion is *free* at `V = ⊥` with
   171	no hypothesis at all (a test point of the empty open forces the test empty, hence initial); and
   172	at general `V` it is `injective_of_isChartUniv` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:205`) composed with
   173	`isChartUniv_of_restrictedChartFibre`, i.e. a property of *any* hypothesis implying `IsChartUniv`,
   174	not evidence about this one.
   175	
   176	The real non-vacuity statement for the assembly is the pair `isChartUniv_bot` /
   177	`not_coverageContainment_bot` in `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`: `⊥` is where this
   178	side is free and the coverage side is impossible, so the two hypotheses cannot both be met at a
   179	convenient `V`.
   180	
   181	Kept because it is the right thing to cite when asking what a producer of the datum must
   182	establish — the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2, over `V` rather than over `D.left`. -/
   183	theorem necessity_of_restrictedChartFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   184	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   185	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   186	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   187	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   188	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V)
   189	    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
   190	    Function.Injective
   191	      ((restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) V).app T) :=
   192	  injective_of_chartFibrePresented _ (fun T' g => (h T' g).some) T
   193	
   194	/-! ## The transport, and what it says about the two halves of the coupling
   195	
   196	An earlier draft of this file priced this transport as "real work needing a pushforward" and
   197	declined to prove it.  **That was wrong** (inbox `I-0936`): no preimage and no pushforward are
   198	involved — keep the old datum's `W` and lift its `r` along `V.ι`. -/
   199	
   200	/-- **`IsChartLocusFibre` plus a range containment gives `RestrictedChartFibre`.**
   201	
   202	And the containment is the *same* one the coverage half owes: `hr` here is character-for-character
   203	the `hV` of `Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.liftPointwiseToOpens`, asked on the fibre side instead of the
   204	coverage side.  So the two halves of the `V`-coupling are **not two obligations** — they are one
   205	range containment asked twice, from opposite directions.
   206	
   207	This is the sharp form of "the restricted datum is weaker", and it is what makes the repair
   208	precise rather than merely differently-shaped. -/
   209	theorem restrictedChartFibre_of_isChartLocusFibre {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   210	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   211	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   212	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   213	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   214	    (V : D.left.Opens) (h : IsChartLocusFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg)
   215	    (hr : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1),
   216	      Set.range (((h T g).some.r).base) ⊆ Set.range ((V.ι).base)) :
   217	    RestrictedChartFibre C π n rep m Z hdeg V := by
   218	  intro T g
   219	  refine ⟨⟨(h T g).some.W, IsOpenImmersion.lift V.ι ((h T g).some.r) (hr T g), ?_, ?_⟩⟩
   220	  · rw [restrictChart, ← Category.assoc, ← yoneda.map_comp, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]
   221	    exact (h T g).some.sq
   222	  · intro S v w hvw
   223	    obtain ⟨u, hu1, hu2⟩ := (h T g).some.exists_factor S (v ≫ V.ι) w (by
   224	      rw [← hvw, restrictChart]
   225	      rfl)
   226	    exact ⟨u, (cancel_mono V.ι).mp (by rw [Category.assoc, IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac]; exact hu1),
   227	      hu2⟩
   228	
   229	/-! ## The `V`-coupled assembly -/
   230	
   231	variable (C π) in
   232	/-- The `hf` clause of a mixed-parameter atlas, from per-index restricted fibre data.
   233	
   234	Named because the representing object of the assembly below mentions it. -/
   235	theorem mixedParamHf {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
   236	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
   237	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
   238	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   239	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)

    16	* `abelDivAffSigma` extends a represented slice map to the ambient big-site presheaf;

    20	`picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C)`, and `DivRankOneOpen` must be an open of
    21	`divRepAffGenusScheme C`. Its `rankOneAbel` is the restriction of
    22	`abelDivAffGenusSigma`, after applying the corresponding Sigma extension. No placeholder locus,

    57	/-- Extend a represented widened Abel map from the slice over `Spec k` to the big site. -/
    58	def abelDivAffSigma {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    59	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) :
    60	    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶
    61	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ)) :=
    62	  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (abelDivAffTrans C n)
    63	
    64	@[simp]
    65	lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_fst {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    66	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    67	    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    68	    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).1 = x ≫ D.hom :=
    69	  rfl
    70	
    71	@[simp]
    72	lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_coe {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    73	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    74	    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    75	    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).2.1 =
    76	      abelDivAff' C n (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom)) (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)) :=
    77	  rfl
    78	
    79	variable (C) in
    80	/-- The ambient genus-degree Abel map on the canonical represented widened divisor scheme.
    81	
    82	This is the map that the future rank-one divisor open must restrict. It is not itself claimed to
    83	be an open immersion. -/
    84	def abelDivAffGenusSigma :
    85	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶
    86	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
    87	  abelDivAffSigma C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C)
    88

     9	/-!
    10	# The universal divisor rank-one open contract
    11	
    12	The genus divisor representer is unconditional, while the rank-one restriction still needs a
    13	family-level open-locus producer.  This file separates those two facts.  The predicate below is
    14	the inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` along the represented universal Abel map.  A
    15	`DivRankOneOpenData` witness identifies that predicate with the range of one actual open of the
    16	representer; only after that witness is supplied do we define the open subscheme.
    17	
    18	This shape prevents a logical `Subfunctor` from being silently reinterpreted as a scheme.  It also
    19	gives the canonical inverse lane a stable contract: it consumes the witness equality and can use
    20	the resulting open inclusion and all of its pullbacks without choosing a generator.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    34	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    35	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    36	
    37	noncomputable section

    39	/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    40	def divRankOneUniversalPredicate :
    41	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    42	  divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi
    43	
    44	/-- Evaluation of the represented genus Abel map on a slice point, with the base morphism
    45	transported from the point in the divisor representer to its source. -/
    46	theorem abelDivAffGenusSigma_app_left_rankOne
    47	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    48	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    49	    (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.left) q.left =
    50	      (⟨T.hom,
    51	        (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op T)
    52	          ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q)⟩ :
    53	        (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
    54	          (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))).obj (op T.left)) := by
    55	  change (⟨q.left ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom, _⟩ :
    56	      (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
    57	        (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))).obj (op T.left)) =
    58	    ⟨T.hom,
    59	      (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op T)
    60	        ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q)⟩
    61	  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext
    62	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) q.w ?_
    63	  let e : Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom) ⟶ T :=
    64	    Over.mkCongr q.w
    65	  let q' : Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom) ⟶
    66	      divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
    67	    Over.homMk q.left rfl
    68	  have hq : e ≫ q = q' := by
    69	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    70	    exact Category.id_comp _
    71	  change (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map e.op
    72	      ((abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app (op T)
    73	        ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q)) =
    74	    (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app
    75	      (op (Over.mk (q.left ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)))
    76	      ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q')
    77	  have hnat := ConcreteCategory.congr_hom
    78	    ((abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).naturality e.op)
    79	      ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q)
    80	  have hhom :
    81	      (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q' =
    82	        (divFunctorAff C (genus C)).map e.op
    83	          ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q) := by
    84	    calc
    85	      (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q' =
    86	          (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (e ≫ q) := by
    87	            rw [hq]
    88	      _ = (divFunctorAff C (genus C)).map e.op
    89	          ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q) :=
    90	        (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp e q
    91	  rw [hhom]
    92	  simpa only [ConcreteCategory.comp_apply] using hnat.symm
    93	
    94	/-- A represented genus divisor lies in the universal predicate exactly when its Abel image
    95	lifts through the single public rank-one Picard locus. -/
    96	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_mem_iff_sigma
    97	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    98	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
    99	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   100	      ∃ v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
   101	          (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (op T.unop.left),
   102	        (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op T.unop.left) v =
   103	          (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) x.left := by
   104	  simp only [divRankOneUniversalPredicate,
   105	    divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter,
   106	    Subfunctor.preimage_obj, Set.mem_preimage]
   107	  let p := (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app T
   108	    ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv x)
   109	  change p ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔ _
   110	  have hleft :
   111	      (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) x.left =
   112	        (⟨T.unop.hom, p⟩ :
   113	          (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
   114	            (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))).obj
   115	              (op T.unop.left)) :=
   116	    abelDivAffGenusSigma_app_left_rankOne x
   117	  constructor
   118	  · intro hp
   119	    refine ⟨⟨T.unop.hom, ⟨p, hp⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   120	    rw [hleft]
   121	    rfl
   122	  · rintro ⟨v, hv⟩
   123	    rw [hleft] at hv
   124	    dsimp [picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl,
   125	      CategoryTheory.Over.sigmaExtensionNat] at hv
   126	    rcases v with ⟨a, y⟩
   127	    dsimp at hv
   128	    have hfirst : a = T.unop.hom :=
   129	      congrArg (fun z => z.1) hv
   130	    cases hfirst
   131	    have hinj := Sigma.mk.inj hv
   132	    have heq :
   133	        ConcreteCategory.hom
   134	            ((PicRankOneOpen pi).ι.app
   135	              (op (Over.mk T.unop.hom))) y = p :=
   136	      eq_of_heq hinj.2
   137	    change p ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T
   138	    rw [← heq]
   139	    exact y.property
   140	
   141	/-- The Yoneda map induced by the inclusion of an open of an object in the slice.  Naming this
   142	map is useful to consumers which need the actual factorisation through the open, rather than only
   143	the proposition that a point lies in its range. -/
   144	def openSubfunctorMap (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
   145	    yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) ⟶ yoneda.obj D :=
   146	  yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι)
   147	
   148	/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.
   149	
   150	Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
   151	Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
   152	def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
   153	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
   154	  Subfunctor.range (openSubfunctorMap D U)
   155	
   156	/-- Unpack range membership into the actual source point and its equality in the ambient Yoneda
   157	functor.  This is the pointwise factorisation API used by inverse constructions. -/
   158	theorem openSubfunctor_mem_iff
   159	    (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens)
   160	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   161	    (x : (yoneda.obj D).obj T) :
   162	    x ∈ (openSubfunctor D U).obj T ↔
   163	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom))).obj T,
   164	        (openSubfunctorMap D U).app T y = x := by
   165	  rfl
   166	
   167	/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.
   168	
   169	The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
   170	preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
   171	is manufactured here. -/
   172	structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
   173	  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
   174	  carrier_eq :
   175	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
   176	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi
   177	
   178	/-- Genuine relative openness of the public Picard rank-one locus produces the universal
   179	divisor rank-one open.  The carrier is the open image of the represented pullback of the Abel
   180	map, and the proof below identifies its Yoneda range with the defining predicate. -/
   181	theorem divRankOneOpenData_of_picRankOneOpen_isOpen
   182	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) :
   183	    Nonempty (DivRankOneOpenData pi) := by
   184	  obtain ⟨X, snd, fst, hpb⟩ := h.rep (abelDivAffGenusSigma C)
   185	  letI : IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   186	    h.property (abelDivAffGenusSigma C) fst snd hpb
   187	  let U := snd.opensRange
   188	  refine ⟨⟨U, ?_⟩⟩
   189	  ext T x
   190	  rw [openSubfunctor_mem_iff]
   191	  rw [divRankOneUniversalPredicate_mem_iff_sigma]
   192	  have hpbT := (IsPullback.iff_app.mp hpb) (op T.unop.left)
   193	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff] at hpbT
   194	  constructor
   195	  · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩
   196	    have hxy : x.left = y.left ≫ U.ι := by
   197	      have hleft := congrArg Over.Hom.left hy
   198	      exact hleft.symm
   199	    have hrange : Set.range x.left.base ⊆ Set.range snd.base := by
   200	      rw [← Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange snd]
   201	      rintro z ⟨t, rfl⟩
   202	      rw [hxy, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]
   203	      change U.ι.base (y.left.base t) ∈ snd.opensRange
   204	      change U.ι.base (y.left.base t) ∈ U
   205	      exact (y.left.base t).property
   206	    let u : T.unop.left ⟶ X :=
   207	      IsOpenImmersion.lift snd x.left hrange
   208	    have hu : u ≫ snd = x.left :=
   209	      IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _
   210	    refine ⟨fst.app (op T.unop.left) u, ?_⟩
   211	    have hcomm := congrArg
   212	      (fun f => (ConcreteCategory.hom f) u) hpbT.1
   213	    change (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op T.unop.left)
   214	        (fst.app (op T.unop.left) u) =
   215	      (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) (u ≫ snd) at hcomm
   216	    simpa only [hu] using hcomm
   217	  · rintro ⟨v, hv⟩
   218	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := hpbT.2.2 v x.left hv
   219	    change u ≫ snd = x.left at hu₂
   220	    have hrange : Set.range x.left.base ⊆ Set.range U.ι.base := by
   221	      rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι]
   222	      change Set.range x.left.base ⊆ snd.opensRange
   223	      rw [Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange]
   224	      rintro z ⟨t, rfl⟩
   225	      refine ⟨u.base t, ?_⟩
   226	      have happ := congrArg (fun f => f.base t) hu₂
   227	      simpa only [Scheme.Hom.comp_apply] using happ
   228	    let V : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   229	      Over.mk (U.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
   230	    let j : V ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
   231	      Over.homMk (U := V) U.ι
   232	    let e : U.toScheme = V.left := rfl
   233	    let l : T.unop.left ⟶ U.toScheme :=
   234	      IsOpenImmersion.lift U.ι x.left hrange
   235	    let l' : T.unop.left ⟶ V.left := l ≫ eqToHom e
   236	    have he : eqToHom e ≫ j.left = U.ι := by
   237	      subst e
   238	      rfl
   239	    have hl : l' ≫ j.left = x.left := by
   240	      dsimp only [l']
   241	      rw [Category.assoc, he]
   242	      dsimp only [l]
   243	      exact IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _
   244	    have hlw : l' ≫ V.hom = T.unop.hom := by
   245	      rw [← j.w, ← Category.assoc, hl]
   246	      exact x.w
   247	    let y : (yoneda.obj V).obj T := Over.homMk l' hlw
   248	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
   249	    change y ≫ j = x
   250	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   251	    exact hl

   253	/-- A named carrier choice for consumers which already possess the Picard openness theorem. -/
   254	def divRankOneOpenDataOfPicRankOneOpen
   255	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : DivRankOneOpenData pi :=
   256	  Classical.choice (divRankOneOpenData_of_picRankOneOpen_isOpen pi h)
   257	
   258	/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
   259	def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
   260	  h.carrier.toScheme
   261	
   262	/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
   263	def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   264	    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
   265	  h.carrier.ι
   266	
   267	theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
   268	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   269	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
   270	  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
   271	  infer_instance
   272	
   273	/- The scheme-level certificate also has the presheaf form consumed by relative-open inverse
   274	   constructions.  This is conditional only on the explicit carrier witness above. -/
   275	theorem divRankOneOpenMap_presheaf_isOpenImmersion
   276	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   277	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)) := by
   278	  exact MorphismProperty.relative_map (divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion pi h)
   279	
   280	/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
   281	divisor functor. -/
   282	def divRankOneOpenOver (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   283	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   284	  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
   285	
   286	/-- The inclusion of the certified open, as a morphism in the slice over `Spec k`.
   287	
   288	This is the map whose Yoneda action is consumed by the canonical rank-one Abel inverse.  Naming
   289	it separately keeps consumers independent of the implementation spelling of `divRankOneOpenOver`.
   290	-/
   291	def divRankOneOpenOverMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   292	    divRankOneOpenOver pi h ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
   293	  Over.homMk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)
   294	
   295	/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
   296	def divRankOneOpenPullback
   297	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   298	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
   299	  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier
   300	
   301	theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
   302	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   303	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
   304	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
   305	  infer_instance
   306	
   307	/-- The arbitrary slice pullback remains an open immersion after passing to Yoneda. -/
   308	theorem divRankOneOpenPullbackMap_presheaf_isOpenImmersion
   309	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   310	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
   311	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf
   312	      (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι) := by
   313	  exact MorphismProperty.relative_map (divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion pi h q)
   314	
   315	/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
   316	theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
   317	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   318	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
   319	    (x : T.left) :
   320	    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
   321	  rfl
   322	
   323	/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
   324	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
   325	    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
   326	  rfl
   327	
   328	/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
   329	theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
   330	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   331	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
   332	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
   333	  h.carrier_eq
   334	
   335	/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.
   336	
   337	The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
   338	replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
   339	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
   340	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   341	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   342	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   343	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   344	      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
   345	  rw [h.carrier_eq]
   346	
   347	/-- A point of the universal rank-one predicate factors through the certified open immersion.
   348	
   349	Unlike a bare range-membership proof, the conclusion exposes the source point and the equality
   350	of its image with the given divisor point, which is the exact data needed by a canonical inverse. -/
   351	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization
   352	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   353	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   354	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   355	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   356	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk
   357	          (h.carrier.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom))).obj T,
   358	        (openSubfunctorMap (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).app T y = x := by
   359	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x, openSubfunctor_mem_iff]
   360	
   361	/-- The same factorisation contract with the named open object and slice inclusion.
   362	
   363	The source in the preceding theorem is definitionally the slice object
   364	`divRankOneOpenOver pi h`; this corollary gives the stable public names expected by inverse
   365	consumers. -/
   366	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization_over
   367	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   368	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   369	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   370	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   371	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver pi h)).obj T,
   372	        (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h)).app T y = x := by
   373	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization pi h x]
   374	  rfl
   375	
   376	/-- The exact inverse-facing factorisation for a point of the represented rank-one preimage.
   377	
   378	The source point is retained as a subtype, so its membership proof is tied to the same divisor
   379	that is factored through `DivRankOneOpenOver`; no unrelated class or top-open witness can satisfy
   380	this endpoint. -/

    16	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` (`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:140`; that file is

    19	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`)

    21	`hD`, `hD'` (effectivity) and `hone` (`h⁰ = 1`).
    22	
    23	**On the chart locus all three are consequences.**  The reason is visible in the definition
    24	and was apparently never read off it: `chartLocus` is *defined* by the very vanishing the rank
    25	anchor consumes.  `IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) asserts, at a point, the
    26	existence of a finite separable `L/κ(t)`, a presenting Čech class `M`, and a `CurveDivisor W`
    27	in that class with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`.  So membership already carries a divisor with
    28	`h¹ = 0`; what it does not carry is that divisor's *degree*, and the degree comes from
    29	outside, from the chart-index constraint.

    31	## The chain, every link landed before this file
    32	
    33	1. `classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff` (`Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean:85`) reads the
    34	   `L`-degree of the presenting class as the plus-degree of the class it presents;
    35	2. the twist ledger (`chartTwist` unfolded through `degAt_mul`/`degAt_inv`/
    36	   `degAt_thetaFamily_pow`/`degAt_sigmaFamily`) turns that into `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`, which the
    37	   chart-index constraint `hdeg` makes exactly `n`;
    38	3. `chi_relCurve_baseField` transports `χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` to the base-changed curve;
    39	4. the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`
    40	   (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives `h⁰ = deg + χ = n + (1 − n) = 1`;
    41	5. `exists_effective_of_h0_pos` (`RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean:175`) then produces an
    42	   **effective** divisor of the same class, so effectivity is free too;
    43	6. `h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` (`RiemannRoch/ClassCohomology.lean:89`) carries the
    44	   `h⁰` value across to it.
    45	
    46	## What this is NOT
    47	
    48	* It is **not** `hb_forces_h0_eq_one` (`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean:180`).  That takes a
    49	  *threshold* hypothesis — every divisor of degree `≥ n` has `H¹ = 0` — which its own file
    50	  proves **false** at `n = g` (a moving degree-`g` family has `h⁰ ≥ 2`).  Nothing here assumes
    51	  a threshold: the vanishing is supplied by the locus at **one** divisor, the one the
    52	  membership witness names.  A statement about one divisor of degree `n` is not a statement
    53	  about all of them, and only the former is true.
    54	* It does **not** discharge `exists_factor`, and therefore closes no antecedent of
    55	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  Everything here is **fibrewise**: it lives over a splitting
    56	  field `L/κ(t)` at a single point `t`.  Per the standing caveat of
    57	  `Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean`, uniqueness of the *fibre* witness is not injectivity of
    58	  the chart at a general test — the gap measured as `RelPicSeparatesDivFamZar`
    59	  (`Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean:237`, also outside this file's closure).  What is removed is
    60	  one *named input* of the field-level keystone, not the relativisation.
    61	* `n = genus C` is **not** proved here and is not assumed either: `n` is whatever the chart
    62	  index is legal at, and `hχ : χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is a hypothesis.  Per `I-1176`,
    63	  `chi_moduleKSheaf` *converts* that pinning rather than supplying it, so the binder stays
    64	  explicit and its supplier stays named.
    65	
    66	## Main declarations
    67	
    68	* `h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg` — the rank anchor at a witness of the pinned degree.
    69	* `exists_splitting_h0_eq_one_of_mem_chartLocus` — **the converse of
    70	  `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`**: from locus membership, a witness with `h⁰ = 1`.
    71	* `eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_of_subsingleton` — the keystone with `hone` discharged.
    72	* `exists_effective_picClass_eq_of_h0_eq_one` — effectivity is free once `h⁰ = 1`.
    73	* `existsUnique_effective_of_mem_chartLocus` — **the payoff**: at a locus point the class has
    74	  an effective representative that is the unique one, with all three keystone binders supplied.

   101	/-- **The rank anchor at a witness of the pinned degree.** -/
   102	theorem h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg
   103	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   104	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
   105	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   106	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   107	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
   108	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
   109	    (n : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   110	    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
   111	    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ))
   112	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
   113	    Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 := by
   114	  have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) W h1
   115	  rw [hW, hχ] at hanchor

   118	/-- **THE CONVERSE OF `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`, WITH THE `h⁰` VALUE READ OFF.** -/
   119	theorem exists_splitting_h0_eq_one_of_mem_chartLocus
   120	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
   121	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
   122	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   123	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   124	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
   125	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
   126	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
   127	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
   128	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
   129	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
   130	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
   131	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   132	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
   133	      -- `M` presents the TWISTED fibre class at `t`: this is what ties the conclusion to
   134	      -- `lam`, `m`, `Z` and `t`, and without it the statement is satisfied by `W = 0`.
   135	      PicEtAff.map C L
   136	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
   137	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
   138	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
   139	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
   140	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
   141	      Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 := by
   142	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
   143	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   144	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   145	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   146	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   147	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   148	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   149	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   150	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   151	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   152	  -- the witness has degree exactly `n`: its class is the presenting class of the twisted
   153	  -- fibre class, whose `classDeg` the ledger computes as `m·d₁ − deg Z = n`.
   154	  have hWdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) := by
   155	    rw [← classDeg_picClass (K := L) W, hWcl,
   156	      classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
   157	    change degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) (Over.testPoint t) = (n : ℤ)
   158	    rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
   159	      degAt_sigmaFamily, hlam, hdeg]
   160	    ring
   161	  -- `χ(𝒪)` transports to the base-changed curve
   162	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ) :=
   163	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L n hχ
   164	  exact ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg,
   165	    h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg n hχL W hWdeg hWh1⟩

   200	field-level content, with every one of the keystone's three binders supplied by the locus. -/
   201	theorem existsUnique_effective_of_mem_chartLocus
   202	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
   203	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)

   205	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   206	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))

   208	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
   209	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
   210	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
   211	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
   212	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
   213	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)

   216	      -- these two clauses the statement is satisfied by `L = κ(t)`, `E = 0` on any curve.
   217	      PicEtAff.map C L
   218	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
   219	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
   220	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
   221	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L E = M ∧
   222	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L E = (n : ℤ) ∧
   223	      0 ≤ E ∧
   224	        ∀ E' : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E' →
   225	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L E' = M → E' = E := by
   226	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
   227	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   228	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   229	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   230	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   231	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   232	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   233	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   234	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   235	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   236	  have hWdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) := by
   237	    rw [← classDeg_picClass (K := L) W, hWcl,
   238	      classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
   239	    change degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) (Over.testPoint t) = (n : ℤ)
   240	    rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
   241	      degAt_sigmaFamily, hlam, hdeg]
   242	    ring
   243	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ) :=
   244	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L n hχ
   245	  have hone : Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 :=
   246	    h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg n hχL W hWdeg hWh1

   248	  obtain ⟨E, hEe, hEcl⟩ := exists_effective_picClass_eq_of_h0_eq_one W hone

   252	    rw [h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq (K := L) hEcl]; exact hone

   256	    fun E' hE'e hcl => ?_⟩
   257	  exact Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one (K := L) hEe hE'e

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocusNative

/-!
# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract

`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The native piece trivializations supply the line-bundle field;
arbitrary-cartesian pushforward base change and the cohomology/rank certificates stay as
explicit obligations.

The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
  CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

/-! ## The native adapter contract -/

/--
A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
cocycle datum.

The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the remaining producer obligations.  The line-bundle
certificate is derived from the canonical piece trivializations, so a field-level H⁰/H¹
calculation or an unrelated line bundle cannot be silently substituted for the native
evaluation module.
-/
structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
  representative : descentClasses C cover
  represents :
    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
  datum_class :
    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
  native_pushforward_base_change :
    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app datum.nativeModule)
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
  h0_rank_one :
    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1

namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation

variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}

/-- Convert the native adapter contract to the existing local-presentation contract.

The two native bridge fields are inserted definitionally; all other fields are transported
without weakening or adding hypotheses.
-/
noncomputable def toLocalPresentation
    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam :=
  { cover := P.cover
    representative := P.representative
    represents := P.represents
    datum := P.datum
    datum_class := P.datum_class
    module := P.datum.nativeModule
    module_iso := P.datum.nativeModuleKSheafIso
    line_bundle := P.datum.nativeModule_isLineBundle
    native_pushforward_base_change := P.native_pushforward_base_change
    h1_vanishing := P.h1_vanishing
    h0_finite := P.h0_finite
    h0_projective := P.h0_projective
    h0_rank_one := P.h0_rank_one }

theorem nonempty_localPresentation
    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam) :
    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :=
  ⟨P.toLocalPresentation⟩

end PicRankOneNativePresentation

/-! ## Immediate rank-one-locus consumer -/

/--
An arbitrary-affine family of native contracts supplies the existing public rank-one-locus
consumer.  The family is quantified in exactly the same way as
`PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition`; the conversion only canonicalizes the module
choice and does not manufacture any of the remaining geometric certificates.
-/
theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_nativePresentations
    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
        Nonempty (PicRankOneNativePresentation pi
          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
  apply mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi
  intro A _ _ t
  obtain ⟨P⟩ := h A t
  exact P.nonempty_localPresentation

end AlgebraicGeometry

variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The collapse on the weaker input

`Pic0ChartSeamCollapse.chartIso_of_seam` derives elementwise injectivity from antecedent 1.
Everything after that step uses only the injectivity, so the same proof runs from it — and
that matters here because the terminal chart has injectivity *without* having antecedent 1
in hand yet. -/

variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

variable (C) in
/-- **The seam collapse from PLAIN INJECTIVITY.**

Verbatim `chartIso_of_seam`'s argument with its first input weakened: instead of
`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f`, which *implies* elementwise injectivity, take the injectivity
itself.  Nothing else in that proof consumes the stronger form.

Recorded separately because the two inputs are genuinely different in strength — that is the
content of `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective` below, which recovers the stronger form
from this one *together with coverage*. -/
theorem chartIso_of_injective {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hinj : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (f.app T))
    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f) :
    IsIso (chartSheafHom C f) := by
  haveI : Presheaf.IsLocallyInjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (chartSheafHom C f).hom :=
    Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_of_injective _ _ hinj
  haveI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (chartSheafHom C f).hom := hcov
  exact (Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso (chartSheafHom C f)).mp
    ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

variable (C) in
/-- **GIVEN COVERAGE, ANTECEDENT 1 IS ELEMENTWISE INJECTIVITY.**

`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion` prices `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` as a two-clause
`MorphismProperty.relative` statement and supplies a fibre-presentation datum
(`ChartFibrePresented`) to discharge both clauses.  This says that in the presence of
antecedent 2 the whole thing is *one* clause: injectivity on points at every test.

The route is the collapse — injective plus locally surjective makes the chart map an
isomorphism of sheaves, and `MorphismProperty.relative` contains the isomorphisms.  So the
fibre-product representability half of antecedent 1 is not an independent obligation for a
lane that already holds coverage.

Note the direction of use.  This is *not* a cheaper route to the seam: it consumes antecedent
2, which the board prices as the most expensive of the three.  What it does is remove
antecedent 1 from the list of things a coverage lane must separately establish, replacing it
with a statement about points.  Combined with `injective_of_isOpenImmersion_presheaf`
(`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion`, the converse, which needs no coverage) the two are
equivalent under coverage. -/
theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_injective {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (hinj : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Injective (f.app T))
    (hcov : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology f) :
    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf f := by
  letI : IsIso f := by
    haveI := chartIso_of_injective C f hinj hcov
    exact (inferInstance : IsIso ((sheafToPresheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (Type u)).map
      (chartSheafHom C f)))
  exact MorphismProperty.of_isIso (P := IsOpenImmersion.presheaf) f

/-! ## The terminal chart at parameter `0`

`abelSigmaChartZero` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUseSite.lean`) is the Abel chart whose
`rep` binder is discharged by `divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy`, i.e. by the degree-zero
producer.  Its representing object is the *terminal* object of the slice, so its source is
`Spec k` and the chart's Σ-component is the identity on points.  That single structural fact
drives both directions below. -/

variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi] [IsIntegral (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left]

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C pi) in
/-- **The Σ-component of the terminal chart's value is the point itself.**

`abelSigmaChart` sends `v` to the Σ-element with structure morphism `v ≫ D.hom`
(`toSigmaExtension_app_fst`), and at parameter `0` the representing object is
`Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec k))`, so `D.hom` is the identity.  Hence reading off the Σ-component
recovers `v` on the nose — no transport, no naturality.

Everything in this section is this lemma read in one of two directions. -/
lemma sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (v : T ⟶ (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))).left) :
    ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app (op T) v).1 = v := by
  change v ≫ 𝟙 _ = v
  rw [Category.comp_id]

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C pi) in
/-- **ANTECEDENT 1'S ELEMENTWISE CONTENT IS UNCONDITIONAL AT THIS CHART**: the terminal chart
is injective on points at every test, with no hypothesis whatsoever.

**Not new content, and the docstring should say so.**  This is the parameter-`0` instance of a
landed arbitrary-`n` lemma in this file's own import closure:
`injective_abelSigmaChart_of_subsingleton rep m Z hdeg divFunctorObjSubsingleton_zero T`
typechecks as a direct replacement for the proof below.  The direct proof is kept because it
exhibits the *reason* — the Σ-component is the point — which is what the rest of this section
consumes; the credit for the fact belongs upstream.

Two points a lane must not misread.

* This is **not** the `V = ⊥` degeneracy of `isChartUniv_bot`
  (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat`) — but **an earlier version of this bullet gave the wrong
  reason**, and the wrong reason matters because it would send a lane looking in the wrong
  place.  It said the distinction is that "here the source is `Spec k`, not the empty scheme".
  That is not it: `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_restrictChart_bot` applies to *this* chart too, so
  the bot degeneracy is available at this source as well.  The real distinction is the **value
  of `V`**: the bot lemmas give antecedent 1 at `V = ⊥`, where by `isChartUniv_antitone`
  (`Pic0ChartVMonotone`) it is *easiest*, and coverage is refuted; what is new here is
  antecedent 1 at `V = ⊤`, unconditionally, where antitonicity makes it *hardest*.
  Antitonicity therefore cannot derive this from the bot results — it runs the other way.
* It is also not in tension with `Pic0ChartForkNegativeBranch`'s refutation of chart-map
  injectivity.  That refutation is at a chart of degree `n` with two distinct effective
  divisors in one class, which needs `2 ≤ h⁰`; at parameter `0` the functor value is a
  singleton (`instSubsingletonDivFamZarSectionZero`), so there is no pair to separate.  The
  fork's negative branch and this lemma live at different parameters, and the fork's own
  hypothesis `2 ≤ Sheaf.h0` is what keeps them apart. -/
-- RENAMED by pic-g (0096 r3), not by this file's author, to unbreak the ROOT build.
-- This theorem was declared here as `injective_abelSigmaChartZero`, which
-- `Pic0ChartMonoUnconditional.lean:82` had already taken for the SAME statement nine hours
-- earlier by a different route (via `injective_abelSigmaChart_of_subsingleton`).  Neither file
-- imports the other, so each compiled alone and the clash appeared only in the root's import
-- closure -- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` failed with "environment already contains".  The suffix
-- names the route used below: the Σ-component of the chart value IS the point.  Nothing else
-- changed, and no external declaration referenced the old name.
theorem injective_abelSigmaChartZero_sigmaComponent (m : ℕ)
    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
    Function.Injective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T) := by
  intro v₁ v₂ h
  have h₁ := sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg T.unop v₁
  have h₂ := sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg T.unop v₂
  rw [← h₁, ← h₂, h]

/-! ## Surjectivity IS the vanishing

The Σ-component being the identity on points means the chart's app is surjective exactly when
the fibre components are forced — and there is at most one thing to hit per structure
morphism precisely when `pic⁰` is a singleton there.  Both directions below are that
observation; neither uses the sheaf property, the site, or a cover. -/

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C pi) in
/-- **Surjectivity of the terminal chart's app, from vanishing `pic⁰`.**

Given a Σ-element `⟨a, ξ⟩` over `T`, the point `a : T ⟶ Spec k` is already a point of the
chart source, and its chart value has Σ-component `a` by
`sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero`.  The two fibre components then live in the same
`pic0Subgroup C (Over.mk a)`, where the hypothesis identifies them — so the transport is
`Over.sigmaExtension_ext` with `Subsingleton.allEq`, and no cohomology, cover or naturality
enters. -/
theorem surjective_app_abelSigmaChartZero_of_subsingleton
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec (.of k)), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S))
    (T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) :
    Function.Surjective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T) := by
  rintro ⟨a, xi⟩
  refine ⟨a, ?_⟩
  refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C)
    (show a ≫ 𝟙 _ = a from Category.comp_id a) ?_
  exact (hvan _).allEq _ _

omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
variable (C pi) in
/-- **THE CONVERSE: surjectivity FORCES the vanishing.**

If the chart's app is surjective at the test `S.left`, then every degree-zero class over
`Over.mk S.hom` — i.e. over `S` itself, since `Over.mk S.hom = S` by `rfl` — is the chart
value of some point, and by the previous lemma's Σ-component computation that point is
`S.hom` itself.  So the class is determined, and two classes over `S` coincide.

This is what makes the decision an equivalence rather than a sufficient condition, and it is
the reason this file's headline is not a weakening: a curve with two distinct degree-zero
classes at one test has no hope at this chart, whatever `V` one restricts to
(`not_seamPair_abelSigmaChartZero_of_two_pic0`). -/
theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_surjective_app
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - ((0 : ℕ) : ℤ))
    (hsurj : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ,
      Function.Surjective ((abelSigmaChartZero (C := C) (pi := pi) m Z hdeg).app T))
    (S : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S) := by
  refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
  -- both classes name a Σ-element over `S.left` with structure morphism `S.hom`
  obtain ⟨vx, hvx⟩ := hsurj (op S.left) ⟨S.hom, x⟩
  obtain ⟨vy, hvy⟩ := hsurj (op S.left) ⟨S.hom, y⟩
  -- the Σ-components pin the two points to `S.hom`, hence to each other
  have hx : vx = S.hom := by
    rw [← sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg S.left vx, hvx]
  have hy : vy = S.hom := by
    rw [← sigmaComponent_abelSigmaChartZero C pi m Z hdeg S.left vy, hvy]
  have : (⟨S.hom, x⟩ : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op S.left)) = ⟨S.hom, y⟩ := by
